newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal H1 profit rises 12 pct to 3.09 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal H1 profit rises 12 pct to 3.09 bln Ffr.

text.p: French cosmetics giant L'Oreal reported on Thursday that its first-half pre-tax profit rose 12.1 percent to 3.09 billion francs ($593 million), helped by an increase in turnover from its foreign acquisitions Maybelline and Jade.
L'Oreal predicted a similar rise in pre-tax profit for the year but signalled a slower rise in net profit, although it said net profit would grow faster than last year's 8.3 percent gain.
Half-year operating profit rose 15 percent to 3.44 billion francs, while revenues climbed 11.7 percent to 30.11 billion.
The group reported nine-month sales rose 12.1 percent to 44.58 billion francs and said it expected a similar sales increase for the full year.

"Growth in (full-year) profit on ordinary activities before taxation, employee profit-sharing and capital gains and losses should equal the rise in sales after allowing for the increase in the group's interest expenses," it said in a statement.
Financial expenses rose to 302 million francs in the first half from 229 million for the year-earlier period, reflecting the cost of the acquisitions made in the second half of 1995.
L'Oreal said net profit before capital gains and losses and after minority interests should rise more than in 1995 despite a higher tax bill and higher payments to minority interests.
Its pre-exceptional profit after minority interests rose 8.3 percent last year to 3.38 billion francs.
The results were issued after the bourse close on Thursday. L'Oreal's stock finished down 0.56 percent at 1,774 francs after having fallen 2.51 percent the previous day.

Analysts attributed the fall to an agency report issued on Wednesday suggesting its full-year profit would not rise as fast as its nine-month sales growth of 12.1 percent. "If that's true, it would be disappointing," one analyst said.
The 1996 consensus forecast for L'Oreal, before adjustment for the interim results, was earnings per share of 56.80 francs, up 12.5 percent from the 1995 result.
